chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala and others, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) emancipated the mischievous ones from his slaves at the time of his death, and retained the good ones. So I said, 'O father! You are freeing these and retaining those.' He said, 'They had been subjected to discipline from me, so this is for that.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Abu Ja'far free the difficult slaves and keep the good ones?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (as) illustrates the practical application of *tadbir* (manumission upon death) within the Ahl al-Bayt's household management, prioritizing the removal of difficult personalities to maintain domestic harmony. The Imam’s explanation that 'this is for this' highlights a reciprocal relationship where the slave's past misconduct justifies the master's financial sacrifice for their freedom, reflecting a nuanced approach to social justice and mercy in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Abdullah Bin Jabala and someone else, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> emancipated (liberated) the mischievous ones from his<sup>asws</sup> slaves, during his<sup>asws</sup> passing away, and retained the good ones of them’. So I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O father<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are freeing these ones and retaining those ones’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They had been subjected to disciplining from me<sup>asws</sup>, so that happened by this’.
en.sarwar: 13. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah and others from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that abu Ja‘far, at the time of his passing away freed the mischievous ones among his slaves and kept the good ones. I asked, ‘Father, do you free these and keep these?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘These were subjected to my disciplining, thus, this is for that.’”
